title: MCP adapter
objective: Agents operate Luxforge through a standards-compliant MCP server, luxforge-mcp, over the existing operation registry: stdio, dual-era (2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25/2025-06-18), a compact default tool profile and generated typed profiles, attaching to the running desktop or an explicit headless owner, with pictures attached inline, Settings › Agents in the desktop, packaging beside luxforge-ctl, a rendered journey and real-client qualification.
context_summary: Settled in the design and decisions: both tool shapes from one generator with compact (luxforge_methods, luxforge_describe, luxforge_call) the default and --tools all or a namespace list for one typed tool per method; preview results carry the JPEG inline by default (at most the 2048 px tier, never exports; --no-images withholds); the running desktop's live session by default, --headless --catalog PATH starting the adapter's own luxforge-json child with Edit authority; a Settings › Agents tab with the binary's path, per-client configuration snippets to copy and the connected live clients with Disconnect. Recorded defaults delegated to the implementer: stdio only, a hand-written synchronous protocol layer (rmcp only as a test client), tool names with . mapped to _, expected_revision optional for asset-revision methods, actor mcp:<client>, no resources/prompts/tasks, a 32-request queue and an 8 MiB image bound. The adapter has no feature logic: schemas come from schema.list, envelopes are built as luxforge-ctl builds them, failures are preserved, mutations are never retried. All tooling stays in Rust: wire conformance is checked against the vendored specification schemas and an independent rmcp client, not the Node conformance suite. On the Linux host, run Clippy, quick and release builds with the pinned 1.94.0 toolchain first on PATH.

tasks.description: Add the registry markers the adapter needs to schema.list: permission-only authority, effect markers on every mutating method, and image result fields.
extra_context: authority: "permissions" on methods that only permission authority may call at all: module.permission.grant, usage.prompt.claim, update.install, update.move-to-applications, catalog.empty-removed (today stated only in notes). A method needing permission authority for one argument value, such as usage.set {enabled: true}, stays unmarked and keeps its note. The marker is taken from the same place the forbidden check is made, or a test holds the two equal, so they cannot drift.

Every mutating method declares reversible: true | false (undoable through history or library undo, or a session or preference change the same operation sets back) and network: true where it can reach the network. A test refuses a mutating method, generated edit.*, mask.*, task.* and query.* included, without an explicit reversible value.

images: [field...] names result fields holding the path of a JPEG the owner wrote for display: preview.read and preview.region, and the corresponding fields of their jobs' results as job.read/job.wait report them, declared per job kind. Never export outputs.

Markers live on the static MethodSpec table and the generated method descriptors; module descriptors gain only what generated methods need. Field names are as stated in the design; their exact placement within the entry is the implementer's.

tasks.description: Add client identity and the connected-client list to the core: session.identify, session.clients and session.disconnect, with connections recorded in the event log; luxforge-ctl identifies itself.
extra_context: session.identify {label}: session-scoped, 1–64 characters, names the calling client; a later call replaces the label.

session.clients: the owner's other registered clients {client_id, label?, authority, transport (loopback | stdio | desktop-internal as applicable), connected_at, last_request_at?, requests}; metadata only, never request contents. The caller and the desktop's own client are excluded.

session.disconnect {client_id}: permission authority only (marked with TASK-001's authority marker if that has landed, otherwise in notes and marked at integration). Closes that client's connection; its session ends exactly as a disconnect ends it today (drafts end, clients jobs it alone wanted stop, a held wait is dropped). Refuses the caller's own id and an unknown id by name.
A connection, identification and disconnection are each recorded in the event log, so a reader such as the Agents tab follows them with events.wait and no polling.
luxforge-ctl sends session.identify {label: "luxforge-ctl"} after its handshake.

tasks.description: Generate JSON Schema 2020-12 input schemas from the parameter vocabulary for every registry method, as a library module in luxforge-cli.
extra_context: Input: a method's schema.list entry. Output: an object schema with properties, required and additionalProperties: false; the envelope never appears. The kind mapping is the design's: integer/number with minimum/maximum, enum, boolean, string with maxLength, text as string with its byte bound in the description (checked by the adapter, not maxLength), identity as the identifier's wire type, points/curve as arrays of pairs with minItems/maxItems, color/artifact/settings/settings-origin in their wire forms, json as {} with its notes, default copied, unit/step/soft range/precision in the description.
An unknown kind is a test failure, not a silent {}.

Also provide the request-side validation the adapter uses before sending (including text byte bounds) and the expected_revision property rules: optional for revision_of asset, required for draft and module-settings.
Add jsonschema, pinned exactly, as a development dependency only, recorded in docs/engineering/dependencies.md and passing cargo xtask audit/deny.

tasks.description: Build luxforge-mcp: the dual-era stdio server with the compact profile, attaching to the running desktop's live session.
extra_context: A third binary in luxforge-cli reusing luxforge_cli::live; the headless-cli repository rule still holds. A reader thread and one worker; requests served in arrival order; at most 32 queued, beyond that a JSON-RPC error naming the limit; incoming lines bounded at 1 MiB.

Modern (2026-07-28): per-request _meta version, capabilities and clientInfo; serverInfo and resultType on results; server/discover; UnsupportedProtocolVersionError -32022 with supported versions; tools/list with ttlMs and cacheScope private, deterministic order; no notifications/message. Legacy (2025-11-25, 2025-06-18): initialize selects legacy semantics for the process, negotiating the client's version or answering 2025-11-25; ping; no resultType. notifications/cancelled drops a queued request or stops the adapter's own waiting at the next hold; it never cancels a Luxforge job.

Compact tools: luxforge_methods {namespace?, query?}, luxforge_describe {methods} (up to 16), luxforge_call {method, params?, expected_revision?}, with the design's annotations. Without a session, methods/describe answer from the built-in registry with source: built-in; calls return no-session or usage (several sessions) as tool errors.

Attach lazily at the first call needing the owner; send session.identify with "<client> via MCP"; mutations use actor mcp:<client name> (≤128 characters) or mcp. Envelopes as luxforge-ctl builds them; expected_revision used when given, otherwise asset.state read on the same connection just before the edit. Never retry; a lost connection reports connection-lost or outcome-unknown (with method and request_id); the next call rediscovers and the first result after it carries a session-replaced warning.

Results: structuredContent plus one text block of the same JSON; Luxforge failures as isError tool results preserving {code, message, data?, job_id?}; unknown tool -32602; schema failures as tool errors naming the parameter; clients-owned jobs warned as luxforge-ctl warns. Fields marked images are read and attached as image/jpeg content, refused above 8 MiB with a warning; --no-images turns attachment off. Flags: --catalog PATH, --tools (compact only in this task; other values refused until TASK-005), --no-images, --help, --version.
Vendor the 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25 schema.json beside the tests with their source URL and licence notice; every message the adapter writes in tests validates against its era's schema.

tasks.description: Add the typed profiles: one generated tool per method for --tools all or a namespace list, with annotations, list-change notifications and an independent rmcp client test.
extra_context: Tool name: the method name with . replaced by _; title: the method name; description: the full notes; inputSchema from TASK-003. A test holds names collision-free and within 64 characters over both registries.
Annotations: readOnlyHint = !mutates, destructiveHint = !reversible, idempotentHint false, openWorldHint = network. Permission-only methods are not offered.

Without a session the list comes from the built-in registry; on attaching, a differing live registry announces a change. With a subscription (modern subscriptions/listen toolsListChanged) or after initialize (legacy), a second live connection holds events.wait and, after events from flags.set or module enablement, rereads schema.list and sends notifications/tools/list_changed when the generated list differs. In headless mode (TASK-006) the adapter rereads only after its own such calls.

rmcp, pinned exactly, is a development dependency of one integration test only, recorded in docs/engineering/dependencies.md: in both eras it lists tools, calls a read and an edit, and receives a list change after a flag change.

tasks.description: Add headless mode: --headless --catalog PATH runs the adapter over its own luxforge-json child.
extra_context: The child is luxforge-json --catalog PATH from beside the adapter's own executable, with Edit authority, never --permission-authority; the adapter speaks JSON lines over the child's stdio through the same client interface as a live connection.
Refuse with a named error when the running-sessions registry names that catalog; a child that fails to start (for example the catalog's exclusive lock) is reported with its stderr, not retried.

The child lives exactly as long as the adapter: on stdin end-of-file close the child's stdin, wait a bounded time, then kill it; forward its stderr to the adapter's stderr. --headless without --catalog is a usage error.
The child is the only owner and the adapter its only client: list changes are re-read only after the adapter's own flags.set or module calls.
